archetype.name: Fringe Contender (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A first-year-coach Raiders team whose efficiency profile, fifth in net EPA, plays like a playoff side. A soft early schedule, a turnover surge and a broken run game keep it a notch below proven.

report.headline: The pass rush and Cousins are real; the turnovers and soft schedule aren't
report.take:
Last year's Raiders were the worst offense in football by EPA and went 3-14. Four games into Klint Kubiak's first season they are 3-1, 4-0 against the spread, and fifth in net EPA. The shape of the team has flipped. It is now built on a defense that gets home, with a 29.9% pressure rate (2nd) and 12 sacks, and on a Kirk Cousins passing game that ranks 7th in EPA per dropback behind a line allowing pressure on just 13.8% of dropbacks. That pairing is the most durable thing here. Pressure and pass protection tend to hold, and both look like scheme and personnel rather than bounce.

The record leans on things that hold up less well. The defense leads the league with nine takeaways and sits 2nd in EPA allowed, but two of its four opponents, Miami and the Chargers, rank 30th and 31st in offense today. The one good offense it faced, Kansas City, scored 30, ran for 189 yards and gave the ball away zero times, and the Raiders lost. The 1.42 wins over expected (4th) says the 3-1 is running about a win and a half ahead of the point differential. History adds a warning: the 2021 team won 10 games on luck it couldn't repeat.

What the numbers hide is a team playing against its own strengths. The run game is close to the worst in the league. Its stuff rate and yards before contact both rank 32nd, rush EPA is negative in every game, and Ashton Jeanty has absorbed 78 carries anyway. Pass rate over expected is still slightly negative. Meanwhile the passing game keeps climbing, from 0.4 pass EPA in Week 1 to 9.8 against the Chiefs. The defense has a matching leak. It wins downfield (5th in deep EPA allowed), but it gives up the short stuff (24th), explosive runs (27th) and red-zone touchdowns on 76.9% of trips (29th). That is why it ranks 2nd in EPA but only 11th in points allowed.

Where this goes depends on whether Kubiak keeps handing Jeanty the ball behind a line that can't block for him, or tilts toward what works. The next five weeks bring New England, then Buffalo, the Rams, San Francisco and Seattle. That stretch will test this defense in a way September didn't. The back end of the schedule is soft enough to keep a wild-card push alive.

strengths.title: A pass rush that wins early
strengths.body: The Raiders pressure on nearly 30% of dropbacks and hit the quarterback at the 2nd-highest rate. That pressure has produced 12 sacks and fed a league-best nine takeaways. Pressure rate is one of the stickier defensive traits, so the rush should travel even as the takeaway count cools. It is also what keeps the deep secondary looking so good.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, efficient Cousins
strengths.body: The line allows pressure on just 13.8% of dropbacks (2nd) and has given up only five sacks. Cousins has turned that into 7th-ranked pass EPA. His best game, 365 yards and 9.8 pass EPA, came against a top-10 Kansas City defense, so this isn't only a product of weak opponents. The 27 QB hits allowed (23rd) is the one crack worth watching.

strengths.title: Nothing gets over the top
strengths.body: Opponents are generating negative EPA on deep throws (5th), and the explosive pass rate allowed is middle-of-the-pack. Pressure forces quick throws before routes can develop downfield. That holds as long as the rush does.

concerns.title: A run game going nowhere
concerns.body: This is a real flaw, not game script. The line ranks 32nd in both stuff rate and yards before contact, so Jeanty is often hit at or behind the line. Rush EPA was negative in all four games, including the 130-yard day against Miami. Losing guard Jackson Powers-Johnson, a 98%-snap starter, for the KC game only makes it harder to fix up front. The bigger question is why the offense still runs slightly more than expected.

concerns.title: Record flattered by takeaways and schedule
concerns.body: Nine takeaways in four games is a pace no defense holds, and the 1.42 wins over expected says the record is ahead of the scoreboard. The elite defensive EPA came mostly against bottom-three offenses. When Kansas City's 5th-ranked offense showed up, the defense had zero takeaways, allowed 189 rushing yards and lost. Expect the EPA allowed to drift toward average as the offenses improve.

concerns.title: Soft underneath and in the red zone
concerns.body: This is partly the cost of an aggressive, rush-first design. Short passes (24th in EPA allowed) and explosive runs (27th) are where offenses find room. The defense bends into touchdowns inside the 20 at the 4th-worst rate in the league. That gap between EPA rank and points allowed won't close on its own.

trend.note: The two units are moving in opposite directions. Pass EPA climbed every week (0.4, 6, 9, 9.8), while points allowed rose from 13 and 14 to 27 and 30 as opponents got better and takeaways went from four to zero.

nextGame.headline: A weak Patriots offense and a thinned secondary suit Las Vegas
nextGame.body:
New England's profile lines up well for the Raiders. The Patriots score 16.3 points a game (30th) and have turned it over far more than they've forced it, at -1.3 per game (27th). That is exactly the kind of offense this pass rush feasted on in September. Their defense is good against the pass (5th in EPA allowed) but 30th against the run. This is the one matchup all year where Jeanty's volume might actually pay off behind a struggling line.

Availability tilts toward Las Vegas. New England is without top corner Christian Gonzalez (95% snaps) and backup corner Channing Canada, has Charles Woods questionable at corner, and is missing DT Christian Barmore. A.J. Brown is on IR and Mack Hollins is questionable, which strips Drake Maye's receiving group further. The Raiders' question marks are Powers-Johnson, who missed KC with a groin injury and is estimated back this week, and Jalen Nailor, who is in concussion protocol. Bech is on IR. The tight ends and Jeanty carry the targets, so a thin wideout room matters less for Las Vegas than it would for most teams.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders pass rush vs Maye's protection
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas pressures at the 2nd-highest rate. New England's line allows a 6.7% sack rate (19th) and holds the ball long, with the 5th-longest time to throw. Combined with the Patriots' turnover problems, this is where the Raiders can steal possessions. It is the clearest edge on the board.

keyMatchups.title: Jeanty against a leaky run defense
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders' run game is 29th in EPA, but New England's run defense is 30th. If the line gets any push with Powers-Johnson back, this is the week the ground game stops being dead weight. If it can't move a bottom-three run defense, the problem is the blocking scheme rather than the matchup.

keyMatchups.title: Cousins vs a Gonzalez-less secondary
keyMatchups.body: New England's pass defense rates 5th, but losing a 95%-snap No. 1 corner, with Woods questionable and Canada out, thins it badly. Cousins has the protection to work the middle to Mayer, Bowers and Jeanty. That means he doesn't need to win outside with a banged-up receiver group.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Raiders lean on Cousins early or keep feeding Jeanty into the line; the split of early-down calls will tell you if Kubiak has adjusted.

restOfSeason.body: The pass protection, the pass rush and Cousins's efficiency look sustainable, and they should keep this team above .500. The takeaway rate, the 4-0 cover streak and the wins over expected will regress. The defense's EPA rank will slide as it meets Buffalo, San Francisco, the Rams and Seattle across Weeks 6-10. That five-game stretch could easily go 2-3, and the run game and red-zone defense will decide how bad it gets. The closing schedule is gentler: the Chargers, Denver twice, Tennessee and Arizona. That gives a real path to a wild card even if the middle of the season bruises them.
swingFactors: Whether the run blocking improves or the offense tilts toward the pass
How the pass rush holds up against the Weeks 6-10 stretch of top offenses
Takeaway regression from a league-leading pace

bets.reason: Las Vegas is 5th in net EPA with a +7.8 point differential, while New England is 16th and -3.0 per game, yet the Raiders are getting more than a field goal. The Patriots are also missing their top corner and a starting DT. Expect some regression from the 4-0 ATS run, but the number still looks a half-point too generous.

The spread and total imply about 24.5 points for a Patriots offense averaging 16.3 (30th). That offense faces the 2nd-ranked pressure defense and the league's takeaway leader, and is short its top receivers. The Raiders' red-zone leakiness is the main risk.

+160 implies roughly a 38% win chance for the team with the better efficiency profile, protection and pass rush in this matchup. The weak NE offense and its turnover problems make an outright upset more plausible than the price suggests.

confidence.note: Four games, weak early opponents and a turnover spike, but the pressure and pass-protection edges are stable.
